discovery: Invention of the quantum cascade laser
motivation: In 1994 Faist, Capasso and Cho demonstrated the quantum cascade laser. It is a new kind of laser in which light comes from electron transitions between engineered subbands in semiconductor heterostructures grown by molecular-beam epitaxy, not from band-gap recombination. Quantum design of the band structure frees the emission wavelength from material constraints and gives compact, powerful and tunable sources across the mid-infrared and terahertz ranges. This region holds the vibrational fingerprints of molecules and was long poorly served by lasers. QCLs and the frequency combs made from them now support trace-gas sensing, environmental and industrial monitoring, astronomy, security, and label-free biomedical spectroscopy, including breath and blood analysis for early detection of disease. The work is a model of curiosity-driven quantum engineering that turned into a powerful technology, and it is a disruptive light-source invention in the tradition the Physics prize honours.
